Rugged tablet for ServiceM8

ServiceM8 is job management software for trades and service contractors, provided by ServiceM8 Pty Ltd, an Australian company whose terms of service put it under Australian law. The UK site describes it as covering the work from the client's first call through scheduling, quoting, job completion, invoicing and payment, names electrical, plumbing, HVAC, cleaning, locksmith, pest control and appliance repair among the trades it serves, and prices plans in pounds from a free tier to £269 a month with a 14 day free trial. The office runs the Dispatch Board in a browser or in a desktop app for PC and Mac; field staff work in the mobile app.

The device question matters more with ServiceM8 than with most job management software, because the vendor built its mobile app for iPhone and iPad first. A limited Android app called ServiceM8 Lite arrived in 2024 for technicians, subcontractors and temporary workers, and the vendor's marketing page still describes it that way. In August 2026 the vendor announced a rebuilt Android app in beta, and when we checked on 19 October 2026 the help centre and the Google Play listing both described ServiceM8 for Android as having almost all the same functionality as the iOS app, with Android 8.0 or higher as the minimum. The vendor's pages are not yet consistent with each other, so this page sets out what each one says.

Below is what ServiceM8 publishes about the devices its apps run on, which Tuga rugged Android devices meet the published Android requirement, what the Tuga W10 can do through the Windows desktop app and a browser and what it cannot, and how a UK sole trader or small firm can buy a single unit to try before kitting out a team.

Requirements

What ServiceM8 needs from a device

Each item below comes from ServiceM8 Pty Ltd's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android app: Android 8.0 or higher, with almost all the same functionality as the iOS app

    The help centre article About the ServiceM8 Android app says ServiceM8 is available for Android with almost all the same functionality as the iOS app, and gives one minimum requirement: Android 8.0 or higher, with a recommendation to keep the app and the operating system up to date. No RAM, storage, processor or screen-size figure is published for Android. The feature list covers schedules, job cards, creating and scheduling jobs, checklists, Forms, photos with annotation, document scanning, PDF quotes and invoices, payments, Proposals, Asset workflows with local barcode lookup, and Clock On and Off. The published differences from iOS are Room Scan and AR, drawing diagrams, editing or filling PDFs from attachment previews, and full in-camera tagging. The vendor's marketing page still calls the Android app ServiceM8 Lite, released in 2024 for staff who do not need the full power of the iOS app, and an August 2026 update post describes a rebuilt Android app as a beta; the help centre and Google Play are the current, more detailed statements. For context, the vendor's iOS compatibility article (updated November 2025) says the iOS app needs iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 or later, and the App Store listing for version 15 states iOS 18.0 or later; the vendor describes the iOS app as its most feature-rich mobile experience. Source: support.servicem8.com

  • Google Play listing: ServiceM8, developer ServiceM8, minimum API level 26 (Android 8.0)

    The Android app is published on Google Play as ServiceM8 (package com.servicem8.skip, developer ServiceM8, with an Australian developer address). When checked on 19 October 2026 the listing showed version 15.0.3, updated 18 October 2026, a minimum API level of 26 (Android 8.0), more than 50,000 downloads, and a description that opens with Run your service business from your Android device and says Android and iOS devices can be used together on one account. The listing we checked did not display a Tablet device chip, and neither it nor the help centre says anything about Android tablet layouts. The vendor's install FAQ tells Android users to download ServiceM8 from Google Play. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working in the mobile app, for data already synced to the device

    The vendor's FAQ says ServiceM8 does work offline in the mobile app: if job and client details have already synced to the device, staff can view them, update jobs and save notes and photos out of reception, and the changes sync when back in range. Tasks that need a live connection still will not work offline: final PDF quotes, invoices and Forms cannot be produced, and emails and text messages cannot be sent, until the device has coverage again. The FAQ refers to the mobile app without naming iOS or Android, and the vendor publishes no figure for how much data is cached. Source: support.servicem8.com

  • Barcode scanning through the camera, in Forms, Assets and Services fields

    The vendor's barcode article says staff can capture barcodes by scanning them into the ServiceM8 app when completing Forms, creating Assets (Asset Management add-on) or answering Service questions. The scan button appears only on Text-type fields whose names contain Barcode, Number, Serial or Model. Tapping it opens the device camera, and the barcode is held inside a green square to scan. The article does not mention QR codes, a dedicated hardware scan engine or an external scanner, and does not name iOS or Android; the Android article lists Asset workflows and local barcode lookup. On any Tuga device the documented scan path is the camera. Source: support.servicem8.com

  • GPS for the Dispatch Map when staff are Clocked On, and NFC only for Tap to Pay on eligible phones

    The vendor says it can show live staff location and status on the Dispatch Map when staff are Clocked On and have allowed GPS access; one FAQ names the iOS app and the Shift GPS report for staff using the iOS app, while the staff status article refers to the mobile app generally. No location accuracy requirement is published. On NFC, the Android article says Tap to Pay requires Android 13 or later, NFC and a phone that meets Stripe's supported-device requirements, that activation is not available in the Android app, and that a phone that can run ServiceM8 does not necessarily support Tap to Pay. The NFC radio on the Tuga A8, A10 and A6 should not be assumed to work for Tap to Pay. Source: support.servicem8.com

  • Windows: desktop app for Windows 10 or higher, or the Online Dashboard in a modern browser

    The vendor publishes a ServiceM8 for Desktop app for PC and Mac, available from servicem8.com/desktop or the Microsoft Store, and says the operating system must be Windows 10 or higher on PC or macOS 10.11 or higher on Mac. It describes the desktop app as the same as using ServiceM8 through Chrome, but faster. The install FAQ says the Online Dashboard needs no installation, only a modern web browser such as Google Chrome or Safari, with no version list. Offline working, camera barcode scanning, Client Signoff and Forms signatures are documented for the mobile app, not for the desktop app or a browser. Source: support.servicem8.com

Worth knowing. ServiceM8's mobile app runs on Android and iOS, not Windows, so the Tuga W10 can only run the ServiceM8 for Desktop app (Windows 10 or higher) or the Online Dashboard in a browser. Offline working, camera barcode scanning, Client Signoff and Forms signatures are documented for the mobile app, so a W10 suits the Dispatch Board on an office or workshop desk, not an engineer on site. On Android, the vendor's own pages disagree on what the app is: the marketing page describes a 2024 Lite app, an August 2026 post describes a rebuilt app in beta, and the help centre and the Google Play listing we checked on 19 October 2026 describe an app with almost all of the iOS functionality. Room Scan and AR, drawing diagrams, editing or filling PDFs from attachment previews, full in-camera tagging and Tap to Pay activation are published as not available on Android, and the vendor still describes its iOS app as the most feature-rich mobile experience; if your business depends on one of those, no Tuga device is the answer. The vendor publishes no RAM, storage or screen-size figure for Android, nothing about Android tablet layouts, and no QR code, dedicated scan engine or external scanner support, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not a documented ServiceM8 input. The NFC radio on the A8, A10 and A6 should not be treated as a Tap to Pay feature. ServiceM8 does not name Tuga devices, and we do not describe any device as certified or tested by ServiceM8.
Setting up

Getting ServiceM8 running

  1. Start a ServiceM8 account at servicem8.com/uk, or ask the account owner to add you as a staff member. The UK site offers a 14 day free trial with no credit card required, and a free plan for one user with 30 jobs a month.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install ServiceM8 (package com.servicem8.skip, developer ServiceM8), then sign in. If a search turns up nothing, the vendor's FAQ says to search for ServiceM8 by name.
  3. Allow location access when the app asks, and Clock On at the start of the shift, because the vendor says staff appear on the Dispatch Map only when Clocked On with GPS access allowed. Allow camera access so barcode scanning, document scanning and job photos work. Fit a data SIM before the first job: offline working only covers jobs already synced, and PDF quotes, invoices, Forms, emails and texts need a live connection.
  4. Before relying on it, run the field flows on the device: open a job card, complete a checklist and a Form, take and annotate photos, scan a barcode into a field whose name contains Barcode, Serial, Number or Model, produce a PDF quote, and collect a Client Signoff signature, so you know how the layout sits on an 8 or 10 inch screen.
  5. Check what your team needs against the vendor's published differences from iOS: Room Scan and AR, drawing diagrams, editing or filling PDFs from attachment previews, full in-camera tagging and Tap to Pay activation are not in the Android app. If one of those is essential, the vendor's answer is its iOS app, not an Android device.
  6. On a Tuga W10, install ServiceM8 for Desktop from the Microsoft Store or servicem8.com/desktop, or open the Online Dashboard in Chrome or Edge and keep the browser updated. Use it for the Dispatch Board and office work; it will not run the mobile app.
  7. For the A8 and A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster or the car phone mount. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.

Questions

ServiceM8 on a Tuga device

It runs on Android, with a history worth knowing. The vendor built its mobile app for iPhone and iPad first, released a limited ServiceM8 Lite app for Android in 2024, and announced a rebuilt Android app in beta in August 2026. When we checked on 19 October 2026, the help centre article About the ServiceM8 Android app and the Google Play listing (version 15.0.3, updated 18 October 2026) both described ServiceM8 for Android as having almost all the same functionality as the iOS app, with Android 8.0 or higher as the minimum. The vendor's marketing page still describes the Lite app, so read the help centre article and its list of differences from iOS before you buy.

The vendor publishes one Android requirement: Android 8.0 or higher, with the app installed from Google Play, where the listing gives a minimum API level of 26 (Android 8.0). The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play, so it meets it, and so do the A10 (Android 14) and the A6 (Android 15). The vendor publishes no RAM, storage or screen-size figure for Android and nothing about Android tablet layouts. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by ServiceM8; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications, so try the app on one unit before buying for a team.

Partly. The vendor says the mobile app works offline for job and client details already synced to the device: staff can view them, update jobs and save notes and photos, and changes sync when back in range. Final PDF quotes, invoices and Forms cannot be produced, and emails and texts cannot be sent, until the device has coverage again. The FAQ does not name Android separately. The A8, A10 and A6 all have dual SIM 4G, so a data SIM, or two, keeps the device synced between Wi-Fi networks. A Tuga W10 runs the desktop app or the Online Dashboard, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

ServiceM8 documents barcode scanning through the device camera, in Forms, Asset and Services fields whose names contain Barcode, Number, Serial or Model, and the Android article lists Asset workflows and local barcode lookup. The A8, A10 and A6 all have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and on each of them scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support and does not mention QR codes, so do not buy the A6 for that reason alone.

Signatures, yes: the vendor documents Client Signoff from the job card, where the client signs on screen and the signature is kept in the job Diary, and a Customer Signature field on Forms that works only in the mobile app; the Android article says separate signature workflows are available on Android. Tap to Pay is different: the vendor says it needs Android 13 or later, NFC and a phone that meets Stripe's supported-device requirements, that activation is not available in the Android app, and that a phone that can run ServiceM8 does not necessarily support Tap to Pay. The A8, A10 and A6 have NFC, but we cannot say they are supported for Tap to Pay, so do not plan on it.

Yes to both. A single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome, and with ServiceM8 it is the sensible route, because the vendor publishes nothing about Android tablet layouts.
